issue: The foundation_only/best.pt checkpoint on Drive was found to have drifted from the originally reported result, likely due to an accidental rerun of training in an earlier session that overwrote the checkpoint file.
verification: The 0.9054 value was independently confirmed twice: once in the original Day-4 run, and again in a Day-5 fresh-recompute audit that matched exactly.
instability_observed: Four separate training runs (same seed=42, same data) produced meaningfully different best-checkpoint test AUROC: 0.9054 (original, twice-verified), 0.9116 (later drifted checkpoint), 0.8785 (fresh non-deterministic retrain during Day-7 verification), and 0.9168 (fresh deterministic retrain during V1.0 hardening pass on Kaggle, with full seeding: random/numpy/torch/cuda seeds, seeded DataLoader, cudnn.deterministic, and torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) all enabled). Because the fourth run remained different from the others despite full determinism, the instability is NOT fully explained by missing seeding alone -- it appears to reflect genuine sensitivity of best-epoch selection to the small validation set (961 samples), possibly compounded by minor environment differences (Colab vs Kaggle library/hardware versions).
resolution: The originally reported and twice-verified value (AUROC=0.9054) remains the official result in README and results/foundation_only_metrics.json. All four runs are preserved as separate evidence (none overwritten or deleted) to document the instability transparently rather than reporting a single cherry-picked number.
recommendation_for_future: Avoid rerunning training cells for already-completed experiments. Consider adding a checkpoint existence check (e.g. raise an error if best.pt already exists and the user hasn't explicitly requested retraining) to prevent accidental overwrites.
